title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 115
paragraphs: The herald accepted the utterance and departed. Xerxes, leaving Mardonius in Thessaly, hurried on himself to the Hellespont, and reached the crossing in thirty-five days, bringing back next to nothing, one might say, of his army. Wherever they came on their march, to whatever nation, they seized the crops of that people and used them for provisions; and if they found no crops, then they took the grass growing from the earth, stripped the bark from the trees, plucked down the leaves, and devoured them — both of cultivated trees and of those growing wild — leaving nothing behind them, such was their famine. Then plague also struck the army and dysentery, which destroyed them as they went; some of the sick the king left behind, charging the cities where at the time he happened to be on his march with their care and support. He left some in Thessaly, some at Siris in Paionia, and some in Macedonia. In those parts he had also left behind the sacred chariot of Zeus when he was marching against Greece, but on his return he did not get it back: the Paionians had given it to the Thracians, and when Xerxes asked for it, they said the mares had been carried off while pasturing by the upland Thracians who dwelt around the source of the Strymon.
